subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a public config-level default task notify policy, and should that policy be global, per runtime, or coordinated with channel-specific visibility rules?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but repository policy treats config/default additions as compatibility-sensitive and related issues show competing needs for suppression, visibility, and per-channel behavior.

options.title: Add per-runtime task defaults
options.body: Introduce an additive `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map that preserves today’s runtime defaults when unset and lets explicit task/flow `notifyPolicy` override it.

options.title: Add one global default
options.body: Expose a simpler global default, but require extra guardrails so cron, CLI, media, and intentionally silent paths do not become noisy by accident.

options.title: Keep per-task controls only
options.body: Decline a config default and keep `openclaw tasks notify` plus targeted owner-specific fixes for Discord, Codex, ACP flood, and announce suppression issues.

recommendation.title: Add per-runtime task defaults
recommendation.body: Introduce an additive `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map that preserves today’s runtime defaults when unset and lets explicit task/flow `notifyPolicy` override it.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest product/config ownership signal among the likely owners and this decision is about public config semantics rather than a narrow code defect.
